title: Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale with LCD Display, Batteries Included, Weighs up to 11 pounds, Black and Stainless Steel
description:
About this item
Digital kitchen scale with food-safe, BPA-free plastic components
Stainless steel platform with wide LCD screen
Weighs up to 11 pounds (2 grams minimum, up to about 5000 grams); displays results in pounds, ounces, grams, fluid ounces, and ml
Tare button for measuring just the food, minus the container weight
Battery operated; (2) AAA batteries included
Product Dimensions: 8.3 x 7 x 1.3 inches (LxWxH)
› See more product details
reviews_5s:
I’ve been using the Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale with LCD Display for several months now, and it has become an indispensable tool in my kitchen. The scale is remarkably accurate, providing precise measurements up to 11 pounds, which is perfect for both baking and cooking needs. The tare function is incredibly convenient, allowing me to zero out the weight of containers and measure ingredients with ease.I love this scale and recommend it highly over the more expensive options out there.
I had a used version of this scale previously, it was a hand me down from a friend who was moving and it lasted me about 5years. When it finally died I upgraded to a more expensive scale but I very realized it was no match for my old one so it got returned and I bought my previous Amazon one again.
It’s made well, easy to operate and read but most important to me is its accuracy, its incredibly accurate no need to set items in one spot wherever it sits on the plate it will weigh accurately. It’s not to big and can easily be stored in a drawer. I’m allergic to gluten but I love sweets so I bake alot and I can easily get accurate measurements in grams or ounces which is important with gluten free baking. I love this scale and it’s honestly 10 x better than the fancy one I first tried so I highly recommend it.This scale works perfectly for my wife and me! I use it to determine how heavy my pickleball paddle is (and how much weight I might want to add to it), and my wife uses it to measure out portions or for recipes that ask for a certain ingredient weight. It's well made, small (so it doesn't take up too much cabinet space, the screen is very readable, and it just looks cool! Good luck!Very accurate. I use grams and it is accurate to a tenth of a gram. Amazing accuracy. Easy to set the tare weight (weight of a container that holds your goods). You only want the weight of your goods, eh. Long battery life. You really more than you expect - the accuracy and repeatability vs the cost of this item. Very nice.This digital kitchen scale has made cooking and baking so much easier! The display is clear and easy to read, and I love that it switches between grams, ounces, and other units with just one button.

It’s lightweight, easy to clean, and looks great on my countertop. I also appreciate the tare function, which lets me zero out the weight of containers.

If you cook often and want more precision in your kitchen, this scale is a must-have. Highly recommended!I am excited to start using this scale. I can use it when cooking, or baking when measuring ingredients for recipes. The easy to see and read digital design makes it a great tool for measuring serving sizes for my diet. This has an 11 lb weight capacity I think but I so far havent needed that. I really like all the functions and love that I can go from gram to lb to oz.

It is perfect for my needs and thus far a really decent kitchen scale.Honestly I'm impressed with the accuracy on this scale, small and practical, make my weighting job a lot easier and I can trust it 100%, it does the job perfectly fine, the best part is the price compared to other expensive scales.The Amazon Basics Digital Kitchen Scale is a fantastic addition to my kitchen! Compact, lightweight, and reliable—this scale is perfect for everyday cooking, baking, and even portion control. Great quality at a great price!I’ve been using this digital kitchen scale and honestly—it’s exactly what I needed.

reviews_1s:
I read through many reviews looking for a new digital food scale to help improve my cooking and meal prep. I thought that between going with an 'Amazon' product and one that was highly prized in reviews would be a safe bet.

I was wrong...

I got only one possibly two useful readings off this scale (I have doubts on whether or not the second one was accurate). Please note that my care for the product includes wiping it down and returning it to be wrapped and stored level in a drawer below counter top. Nothing is stored on it, nor do I lift it in any other way than level. After being curious as to why the weight seemed off (weight actually reduced after putting additional item on scale) I recognized that the scale itself was dislodged in the front, and resting unevenly in the back. I have tried gently twisting, tapping, even inverting to see if it would reset itself but to no avail.

I will likely be buying a different one in the near future.... but I have learned my lesson with Amazon Basic Products.... AVOID!!The Amazon Basics kitchen scale is a marvel of poorly designed kitchen tools. My main gripe with this scale is it's auto-off feature. Like any sane home chef, I leave my scale on while I add things to my bowl, or while I steep my pour-over coffee. The scale decides when it turns off to save all that precious AAA battery power outputting info on that tiny, non-backlit 3.5" LCD display, and there is zero consistency on when it decides to turn off. So, all my weighing gets erased, and I either have to start over or pee into the wind and hope my measurements are accurate moving forward.

3 stars for accuracy, because it managed to do the bare minimum and give me at least some information before saying, "Welp, that's enough weighing for me" and then clock out for the day after two minutes of screen-on time. I hate this scale with a fiery passion, and I hope J.ef.f B.ez.os enjoys the $6.50-or-whatever-revenue from my purchase.

Bonus gripe: there is a volume feature on here, where the scale measures in mL or fl oz. Why? Why would a scale measure volume? What good would it be for anything denser than water, oh wise Amazon Basics scale? Are you trying to do too much for a $10 kitchen item? I bought this so could weigh things, Amazon, why are you implementing a feature on a tool for which it wasn't even designed? If I wanted to measure out volume, my first thought would sure as hell NOT be a kitchen scale, because I passed the 6th grade.

For the love of all that is good and holy: do not buy this scale, spend a little more, and get a kitchen scale that is worthwhile, so you don't have to write an Amazon review like this.After I bought it, someone on a baking show mentioned that he would not recommend it. I should have returned it then, but thought maybe his was an exception.
Mine is also poorly made and malfunctioned after a few uses. I bought it three months and from the first use, it was difficult to turn it off. You have to press the off button for a long time to turn it off. Then after using it only once a week for this period, it started to malfunction in the weight. You weigh one item and by the time you add another, the weight number of the first starts to automatically decrease. This means I cannot trust that it weighs items accurately. Therefore it is USELES. I wish I could return it, but it is past the return date.I really wanted to like this scale. I loved everything about it until the display screen started producing broken, unreadable numbers just three days in. Really too bad.

I *suspect* that when a bit of water splashed on the surface, it got in the crack where the button is seated. I really mean just a few drops that unfortunately did fall smack on that right button, but that seems to have been enough to kill it. It's a good scale, it needs to be able to handle a bit of powder and liquid on the surface in my opinion.I was using this product mainly to help me in my cooking and baking, and I found it could not reliably measure 1 gram or .5 grams, which is a spice measurement I needed in order to make mixes. It seems that if you add the item gradually and it's pretty light (in the range of 0-5g) then the scale will consistently "tare" and resetting to 0 until it's a gram amount it can no longer ignore, and then will immediately go to 5 grams or higher.

When I was trying to work around this, I thought I'd double / triple the masala recipe so I could use higher gram amounts to not confuse the scale, but even then, it struggled to measure consistently in the 400-500 gram ranges for other powdered spices. I could use the same bowl, press the Tare button, and put in the same amount of masala, and it would give me a different random number within 20 grams range (i.e. 491, 512, 487). It's really frustrating to use.I bought this last July to use at work. I'm diabetic and it's useful to me to measure out servings of snacks but especially coffee creamer. I can't eyeball the amount I want, but using and washing measuring spoons at work would be annoying. The scale it is. I have a kitchen scale at home from Etekcity that is just one solid piece, and that's what I should have gotten here. I don't store the scale out on my desk. I use it to weigh out my creamer and then put it in a drawer. I'm assuming something about moving it like that loosened the top section. I don't know but here it is six months later and the dang thing is no longer functioning, and the top bit is wobbly and there is nothing I can do about it. It was a total waste of money. I am replacing it with the Etekcity.I ordered this scale after reading multiple good reviews. I thought it would be good for home use based on what I read, but I did not have the same experience. The scale is poorly constructed and incredibly inaccurate. The weight of the food changes drastically based on which part of the scale it is placed. Food placed toward the back half of this scale can weigh in the negatives. Even when using a bowl and centering the food, you can weigh the exact same thing and get very different measurements. I would not recommend it, but maybe I just got a defective scale. I will be looking at another brand for my next scale.It’s not accurate. I’m not using it for food but I did test it with multiple things that say their measurements and they are off. I just checked with the fluid oz with a rockstar because it’s what I have. When I tare out the can, it still measures as 17.5 fl when it’s listed as 16 fl oz. I did need this with limited funds but I think I’m going with something different.Disappointed that the unit was not more precise. I now know what to look for in a scale and searched reviews for one that appeared to work well to the grams. Obviously, 3x the price point but it was worth it to me. If you need a basic scale for rough estimates, then this would be fine. Otherwise, I suggest you look around. Love purchasing thru Amazon, they make it so easy to figure this all out and returns are a breeze!The scale began booting up to a test/error screen and would not reset to zero. There is supposed to be an option to replace it but the website only shows you self-repair steps.
